prompt:
Write 8 short claim log entries (one to three sentences each) by an auto insurance adjuster for a hit while turning left claim, in time order. Injury: shoulder injury. The claimant is not represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1175; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury matches the kind and force of the crash well.
- Treatment ran somewhat longer than usual for this injury.
- No earlier injury to the same body area is known.
- Photos confirm some details, but there are no independent witnesses.
- The vehicle damage matches the described impact.
- The claimant told the same account in every conversation.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- A neighbor thinks the car was damaged some weeks before the claimed date.
- The driver lives with the policyholder and is covered as a household member.
text:
Entry 1: Claim received for a collision in which the insured vehicle was struck while turning left at an intersection. The claimant reports a shoulder injury and is not represented by an attorney.

Entry 2: Reviewed the photographs submitted with the first notice of loss. They show damage consistent with the described impact, and the repair estimate lines up with the areas affected.

Entry 3: Spoke with the claimant, who gave the same account of the collision as in the initial report. Confirmed through the police report and a witness statement that the claimant was seated in the vehicle at the time.

Entry 4: The claimant's medical records describe a shoulder injury that fits the kind and force of this crash. Treatment has continued somewhat longer than is typical for this injury, so the file will be monitored.

Entry 5: No prior injury to the same shoulder appears in the claimant's history or in available records. Requested prior claims history to confirm.

Entry 6: No independent witnesses to the collision have come forward, and the photographs are the only independent confirmation of the details at this stage.

Entry 7: A neighbor mentioned seeing the car with damage some weeks before the reported loss date. Noted the comment for follow-up, and no earlier damage to the vehicle is currently on record.

Entry 8: The driver lives with the policyholder and qualifies as a covered household member under the policy. Coverage confirmed, and the file remains open pending the neighbor follow-up and final medical review.
